\int x^{2} e^{x^{3} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "1d738089-1b16-575b-8c40-65a64421bffd" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{3} + 2$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int x^{2} e^{x^{3} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=e^{u}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int e^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(e^{u}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{e^{x^{3} + 2}}{3}+C.
